items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the state finance law and the real property tax law, in
relation to authorizing certain municipalities in a pilot emergency repair
program to add unpaid emergency repair charges and housing code violation
penalties, costs and fines to such municipalities' annual tax levy in
accordance with applicable law; and providing for the repeal of certain
provisions upon the expiration thereof
items.lawCode: Amd §54-g, St Fin L; add §903, RPT L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8146

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the state finance law and the real property tax law, in
relation to authorizing certain municipalities in a pilot emergency
repair program to add unpaid emergency repair charges and housing code
violation penalties, costs  and fines to such municipalities' annual tax
levy in accordance with applicable law; and providing for the repeal of
certain provisions upon the expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To create a pilot emergency repair program to allow cities to directly
address code violations where the owner has not undertaken repairs.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Directs that the Secretary of State receive additional fund-
ing from the state to support a pilot program for activities related to
the administration and enforcement of the fire prevention and building
codes. The program will permit participating municipalities to imme-
diately repair hazardous code violations in buildings where the owner
has not undertaken repairs, and permit them to bill the owner for repair
costs. In the event payment is not received within thirty days, the
secretary shall reimburse the municipality for such repairs. The State
then will be forwarded monies due from the owner for such repairs once
they are collected.  Only municipalities designated as a city will be
eligible to participate in the pilot program.

Section 2: Outlines the guidelines of the pilot program.

1) Authorizes participating municipalities to collect unpaid emergency
repair charges, housing, building, and fire code violation penalties.

2) Outlines that eligible charges, penalties, costs, and fines must be
imposed through a judgment in court and must have remained unpaid for
one year after the final adjudication and exhaustion of all appeals.

3) Sets minimum amount to be eligible for program: at least five percent
of the amount of the tax assessed value of the property.

4) Directs that the unpaid charges be set down in the annual tax levy as
uncollected fines and penalties.

5) Directs that the participating municipality must notify all owners or
known interested parties of unpaid emergency repair charges and/or code
violations on the municipal tax levy as uncollected fines and penalties
within thirty days of placement.

6) States that unpaid emergency repair charges shall be placed on the
tax year that the municipality is currently in.

7) Exempts a residential dwelling that is owner-occupied or is the
primary residence of a homeowner from the program.

8) Directs that the participating municipality shall develop a program
to assist tenants residing in a dwelling at risk of tax foreclosure
before placing a property on the tax levy. Program will include housing
counseling assistance or other relocation support to suitable housing.

9) Permits creation of payment plans for owners with participating muni-
cipality for past amounts due for emergency repair charges and/or code
violations.

10) Outlines curing code violations: if all violations that led to
penalties, fees, and costs are corrected prior to the expiration period
for redemption, then the property shall be removed from the levy and
auction and balance of amount owed will be placed as a lien on the prop-
erty.

11) States that a property may not be auctioned and will be removed from
the tax levy should the outstanding balance be paid on a property's
emergency repair costs and if there are also no unpaid real property
taxes.

12) States that any surplus funds from a sale of a property at a tax
foreclosure for unpaid code violations shall be returned to the former
owner of the property. This provision does not apply to sales of proper-
ty at a tax foreclosure due to unpaid taxes.

13) Should there be emergency repair charges and/or code violations
still due after the auction of the property, the municipality may
proceed with action against the former owner pursuant to applicable
laws.

14) Excludes municipalities that sell their tax liens in a tax lien sale
to the provisions of the program.

Section 3: Sets effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Around New York State there are a properties in cities that have been
issued code violations by the jurisdictional municipality but continue
to be in a state of disrepair either due to negligence or unwillingness
by the owner to make the necessary repairs. This can create extreme
safety issues to renters who reside at the property and slowly deteri-
orates property values in the surrounding neighborhood.

This bill seeks to remedy this issue by creating a program that would
authorize participating municipalities to make direct code enforcement
repairs that the landlord has either failed or refused to do. The muni-
cipality places the cost of the emergency repairs on the landlord's
property tax bill as a lien, with the state providing the municipality
with the upfront costs of the repairs and recouping the money upon reme-
dy of the lien/violations. A similar program currently exists in NYC
under its Housing Preservation and Development's Alternative Enforcement
Program through issuing of Orders to Correct.

The pilot program created by this bill will last until May 1, 2026.
During which the secretary of state in conjunction with the division of
housing and community renewal will file a report annually to evaluate
the effectiveness of the pilot program with the legislature and the
governor.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, section one
of this act shall expire and be deemed repealed May 1, 2026
